target.title: fix(qqbot): require own account credential entries
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where QQBot logout/setup credential cleanup could treat prototype-inherited named account entries or inherited credential fields as if they were explicit user config. In affected programmatic config shapes, logout could either report cleanup for config the user did not own or continue resolving an inherited account as configured after cleanup skipped the write.

## Why This Change Was Made

QQBot credential cleanup now uses own-property checks across the whole logout/setup account path, not only the low-level credential remover. Named account resolution, default-account selection, setup account updates, bridge account resolution, and credential clearing now agree that only own `channels.qqbot.accounts.<id>` entries and own `clientSecret` / `clientSecretFile` fields are mutable user config.

## User Impact

QQBot logout and setup cleanup now ignore prototype-inherited account data and only clear credentials that are actually present on the user's config object. Normal own account logout still removes `clientSecret` / `clientSecretFile`, keeps non-secret fields such as `appId`, and writes the cleaned config through the existing runtime path.

## Evidence

Exact head: `2bb5d5dade24d41b2ba5b6898991c026ad81ce11`

- Focused regression tests: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/qqbot/src/engine/config/credentials.test.ts extensions/qqbot/src/channel.logout.test.ts` passed, 6/6 tests.
- Test typecheck: `node scripts/run-tsgo.mjs -p test/tsconfig/tsconfig.extensions.test.json --incremental false --pretty false` passed.
- Gateway logout proof: exact-head `qqbotPlugin.gateway.logoutAccount` was exercised with a redacted inherited-only named account and a redacted own named account. Output is below.
- Format: `node_modules/.bin/oxfmt --check --threads=1 extensions/qqbot/src/engine/config/resolve.ts extensions/qqbot/src/bridge/config.ts extensions/qqbot/src/channel.logout.test.ts extensions/qqbot/src/engine/config/credentials.ts extensions/qqbot/src/engine/config/credentials.test.ts` passed.
- Lint: `node_modules/.bin/oxlint --threads=1 extensions/qqbot/src/engine/config/resolve.ts extensions/qqbot/src/bridge/config.ts extensions/qqbot/src/channel.logout.test.ts extensions/qqbot/src/engine/config/credentials.ts extensions/qqbot/src/engine/config/credentials.test.ts` passed.
- Whitespace: `git diff --check` passed.
- Fresh autoreview: `env -u OPENAI_API_KEY -u OPENAI_ORG_ID -u OPENAI_PROJECT_ID .agents/skills/autoreview/scripts/autoreview --mode local` exited 0 with no findings.

## Real behavior proof

The proof drove the QQBot gateway logout entry point with a runtime `replaceConfigFile` capture. It did not call the private helper directly.

```text
scenario=inherited-named-account
resolvedBefore.secretSource=none
result={"ok":true,"cleared":false,"envToken":false,"loggedOut":true}
writes=0
runtime-write: yes
scenario=own-named-account
resolvedBefore.secretSource=config
result={"ok":true,"cleared":true,"envToken":false,"loggedOut":true}
writes=1
```

Why this covers the blocker: before the follow-up fix, the same gateway-level proof resolved the inherited-only named account as `secretSource=config` and returned `loggedOut=false` even though cleanup skipped the write. At this head, inherited entries are ignored end-to-end, and own credentials still go through the normal config write path.

Proof boundary: live QQBot traffic was not used. The proof exercises the real QQBot plugin logout/setup cleanup boundary with redacted config objects and a captured runtime write path; no QQBot token, app secret, or external API call is involved.
